question: In which year was the microfinance movement formally launched in India on a pilot basis?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The microfinance movement in India was formally launched in **1992** on a pilot basis by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD).
 
• This initiative focused on linking **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** to banks, enabling better access to financial services for the rural poor.
 
• It aimed to provide **credit and savings facilities** to people in rural areas who lacked access to formal financial institutions.
 
• The **Self-Help Group-Bank Linkage Program (SHG-BLP)** was the cornerstone of this microfinance movement in India.
 
• By the end of the 1990s, this model of microfinance gained momentum and became one of the largest microfinance initiatives globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs):**

 
 
• SHGs are informal associations of people who come together to address common financial and social issues.
 
• They pool small savings from members and use the funds for lending within the group.
 
• SHGs play a vital role in promoting financial inclusion and women's empowerment in rural India.
 
 
 
• **NABARD:**
 
 
• The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) is a development bank focused on rural development in India.
 
• It was established in **1982** to provide credit and financial support to agriculture and rural sectors.
 
• NABARD spearheads several programs, including the SHG-BLP, to promote financial inclusion.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance:**
 
 
• Microfinance refers to providing financial services like loans, savings, and insurance to the economically disadvantaged.
 
• It aims to reduce poverty and empower individuals by enabling them to become financially self-sufficient.
 
• Globally, organizations like Grameen Bank in Bangladesh are known pioneers of microfinance.
 
 
 
• **Significance of SHG-BLP:**
 
 
• The SHG-Bank Linkage Program has been instrumental in extending financial services to millions in rural India.
 
• It is one of the largest microfinance programs globally, involving commercial banks, regional rural banks, and cooperative banks.
 
• The program has contributed significantly to poverty alleviation and rural development.
